lessons.notes_html:
First Day in Class III - My Speech: Pre-reading, While-reading and Post-reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: What is your favourite subject?
    Ans: Sample answer: My favourite subject is English. I like to speak with my friends in English and to learn new words through games and activities, as the speaker does in the speech.
  • Q: Pre-reading: Do you like your school? Give reason.
    Ans: Sample answer: Yes, I like my school. I come to school every day to learn new things, and it is fun to learn and play in the school with my friends.
  • Q: While-reading: Do you want to add something to your speech?
    Ans: Sample answer: Yes. I want to add that we should listen to our teachers, follow the class rules, and keep our classroom clean so that we always stay healthy and happy.
  • Q: Post-reading: There are three paragraphs in the speech, which one do you like the most?
    Ans: Sample answer: I like the last paragraph the most. It tells us about a very important rule, to keep our classroom clean, and it says this habit will help us to keep our school and home clean and to always be healthy and happy.
  • Q: Post-reading: Name two rules for your classroom which you will always follow.
    Ans: Sample answer: Two rules I will always follow are: 1) Listen when others are talking. 2) Keep your classroom clean. The poster in the speech also gives rules such as follow directions, work quietly and do not disturb others, and show respect for school and personal property.

Reading Comprehension

  • Q: What makes you happy on the first day of new class?
    Ans: Sample answer, from the speech: Meeting all my friends makes me happy on the first day of the new class. The speaker says, 'Today is my first day in class III. I am very happy. All my friends are also very happy.'
  • Q: Is it important to listen to your teachers? Give a reason.
    Ans: Yes, it is important to listen to our teachers. The speech says, 'We listen to our teachers,' and 'My teachers help me to learn through games and activities.' Listening to them helps us learn new things.
  • Q: How will you keep your class clean?
    Ans: I will keep my class clean by using the things named in the speech: brush, mop, water bucket, duster, liquid soap and a sign board to show if the floor is wet. This habit will help us keep our school and home clean.
  • Q: Which rules help you to learn English language?
    Ans: Sample answer: Listening when others are talking and speaking nicely help me to learn English. The speaker says, 'I like to speak with my friends in English,' and the class rules include listening to others and following directions.
  • Q: Write two important rules for your classroom and share these in the class.
    Ans: Sample answer: 1) Listen when others are talking. 2) Keep hands, feet and objects to yourself and work quietly and do not disturb others. These rules are given on the Class Rules poster in the speech.

Analytical Reading

  • Q: Read the list and tick the rules which you have experienced in your earlier classes (Class I and Class II): Raise your hand before you speak, Use polite words, Help others, Listen when others are speaking, Have fun, Work together
    Ans: Sample answer: All six rules are followed in Classes I and II, so all can be ticked for both classes: Raise your hand before you speak, Use polite words, Help others, Listen when others are speaking, Have fun, and Work together. A student's own ticks may differ according to his or her experience.

Oral Communication - Learning the Sounds

  • Q: Listen and circle words with soft sound of 'c'. Words: fence, cat, can, dice, cap, case, cow, cycle, cute, cake, mice, court
    Ans: The words with the soft sound of 'c' are: fence, dice, cycle and mice. In these words c is followed by e, i or y, so we pronounce the soft sound. The other words have the hard sound of 'c'.
  • Q: Listen and circle words with soft sound of 'g'. Words: gold, germ, gram, pigeon, page, German, grass, giant, grant, grain, orange, ring, ginger
    Ans: The words with the soft sound of 'g' are: germ, pigeon, page, German, giant, orange and ginger. The other words have the hard sound of 'g'.
  • Q: Make two more words with the cluster 'sh'.
    Ans: Sample answer: shop and shoe. The book gives ship, shirt and shrub in the initial position and dish, fish and brush in the final position.
  • Q: Make two more words with the cluster 'st'.
    Ans: Sample answer: star and stone. The book gives stop, stamp, stick and study in the initial position and dust, must, first and crust in the final position.

Learning to Speak

Vocabulary Building

    Ans: Syllabic division: learn (1 syllable). Meaning: gain knowledge of or skill by studying.
  • Q: Write the syllabic division and meaning of 'through'.
    Ans: Syllabic division: through (1 syllable). Meaning: from one side to another.
  • Q: Write the syllabic division and meaning of 'activity'.
    Ans: Syllabic division: ac-tiv-i-ty (4 syllables). Meaning: a thing that a person or group does.
  • Q: Write the syllabic division and meaning of 'poem'.
    Ans: Syllabic division: po-em (2 syllables). Meaning: a piece of writing with rhythm.
  • Q: Write the syllabic division and meaning of 'fun'.
    Ans: Syllabic division: fun (1 syllable). Meaning: enjoyment, amusement, or pleasure.
  • Q: Write the syllabic division and meaning of 'poster'.
    Ans: Syllabic division: pos-ter (2 syllables). Meaning: a large printed picture used for decoration.
  • Q: Write the six words (learn, through, activity, poem, fun, poster) in alphabetical order.

Grammar

    Ans: Proper noun: Pakistan (name of a specific country, begins with a capital letter). Common noun: country.
  • Q: Underline Proper nouns and circle common nouns: My sister's name is Maryam.
    Ans: Proper noun: Maryam (name of a specific person, begins with a capital letter). Common nouns: sister, name.
  • Q: Underline Proper nouns and circle common nouns: I like chocolate ice-cream.
    Ans: There is no proper noun in this sentence. Common nouns: chocolate, ice-cream.
  • Q: List five proper nouns and five common nouns from your surroundings.
    Ans: Sample answer: Proper nouns: Pakistan, Maryam, Ali, Allama Iqbal, Peshawar. Common nouns: girls, boys, classroom, teacher, school. The book gives Allama Iqbal and Pakistan as proper nouns and girls, boys and classroom as common nouns.

  • Q: Write the number of syllables and syllable division of 'happy'.
    Ans: 2 syllables: hap-py.
  • Q: Punctuate the lines by using capital letters, commas, inverted commas and exclamation marks: hello everyone today is my first day in class III i am very happy all my friends are also very happy
    Ans: "Hello everyone! Today is my first day in class III. I am very happy. All my friends are also very happy." Capital letters begin each sentence and the proper naming in class III, full stops end the sentences, inverted commas show the speech, and the exclamation mark after 'everyone' shows excitement.

Creative Writing

  • Q: Study the given mind-map 'My Classroom' and add information where needed: Lessons in a day, Name of English Teacher, Furniture, Number of students boys + girls, List of fun activities, Describe the classroom big/small
    Ans: Sample completed mind-map: My Classroom is a big classroom. It has desks, chairs, a blackboard, charts and posters as furniture. Boys and girls study together in it. We have lessons in different subjects in a day. Our English teacher teaches us through games and activities. Our fun activities are reading poems, singing and playing games. A student's own names and numbers will be different.
  • Q: Write six lines on 'My Classroom'. Remember to use correct capitalization, punctuation and spellings.
    Ans: Sample answer (six lines): My classroom is big and clean. There are boys and girls in my classroom. We have desks, chairs, charts, posters and a map in our room. Our English teacher helps us to learn through games and activities. We listen to our teachers and follow the class rules. I love my classroom and I keep it clean.

lessons.notes_html:
Golden Sun: Pre-reading, While-reading and Post-reading

  • Q: Pre-reading: While coming to school which different things do you see?
    Ans: Sample answer: While coming to school I see birds, plants, trees, flowers and fields, and the sun shining in the blue sky. The poem also names bird, plant, flower and field as things that depend on the sun.
  • Q: Pre-reading: What objects of nature do you like the most?
    Ans: Sample answer: I like the sun the most. The poem calls it the great, glorious, golden sun and says it is the life of all this earth.
  • Q: While-reading: What is important for bird and plant?
    Ans: The sun is important for bird and plant. The poem says, 'You are the life of bird and plant, All must depend on you.'
  • Q: Post-reading: List the gifts we get from the sun.
    Ans: From the poem, the gifts we get from the sun are its light and its magic ray. It gives life to all this earth, to bird and plant, and it shines down on flower and field the whole day long.
  • Q: Post-reading: What does life on earth depend on?
    Ans: Life on earth depends on the sun. The poem says, 'You are the life of all this earth,' and 'You are the life of bird and plant, All must depend on you.'

Reading Comprehension

  • Q: Which colour has been mentioned in the title of the poem and why?
    Ans: The colour golden has been mentioned in the title 'Golden Sun'. The sun shines with a golden light, and the poem begins, 'Great, glorious, golden sun, Shine down on me today.'
  • Q: Sunlight is a blessing. How?
    Ans: Sunlight is a blessing because the sun is the life of all this earth. Bird and plant depend on it, it shines on flower and field, and it gives us its light forever, as the poem says, 'Forever and ever give us your light.'
  • Q: What does the poet feel about the sun?
    Ans: The poet, Lenore Hetrick, loves and admires the sun. She calls it great and glorious, asks it to shine down the whole day long, and says, 'And never say goodbye.'

Analytical Reading

  • Q: Read the poem 'Moon' and compare it with the unit poem 'Golden Sun'.
    Ans: 'Golden Sun' is about the sun in the day. The sun is golden, it shines from the blue sky, and it is the life of bird, plant, flower and field. 'Moon' is about the moon at night. The moon is silvery, it is seen on a windy night flying so fast, and the frosty stars race past chasing her. So the sun gives golden light in the day and the moon gives silvery light at night.

Vocabulary Building

    Ans: My name is Bano. I live in a small house. I call it a 'Happy Home'. I have an elder sister and a brother who is younger than me. My parents take good care of us. My grandparents also live with us. My house has three rooms, a kitchen and a family room. There is a small garden in front of the house. I love to water the plants in the evening. I also keep a white kitten as a pet. I call it 'kitty'. At home, I respect everyone, help my parents to keep the house clean and tidy, and share my routine with my parents. I do not meet strangers, do not accept eatables or gifts from them, and do not go outside my home without permission.

D) Writing — 1. Learning to Write: Story Writing

  • Q: Re-tell the story (Kindness to Children) by writing one sentence each of the mind map: Beginning, Middle, End, Characters, Place, Time. Give it a title.
    Ans: Title: Kindness to Children. Characters: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him), Hazrat Imam Hassan, Hazrat Imam Hussain and the children. Place: At the Friday sermon and at home. Time: Once, on a Friday. Beginning: Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) loved children and taught us how to treat them well and express our love and joy for them. Middle: Once he was giving the Friday sermon and he saw his grand children Hazrat Imam Hassan and Hazrat Imam Hussain coming towards him; their shirts were too long and they fell, and he got up and rushed to pick them up, and he would give the first fruit of the season to the youngest child present there. End: The life of the Rasool (peace be upon him) is a complete guidance for all of us, so we should treat every child with love and kindness.

D) Writing — 2. Creative Writing

  • Q: Write a story on a zoo elephant with the given points: Babloo, an elephant from Lahore zoo — likes to eat peanuts, popcorns — feels happy to get food — children love it for rides — fresh after taking bath.

lessons.notes_html:
Pre Reading

  • Q: What do you see on the roads early in the morning?
    Ans: Early in the morning all human activities start. People rush to their workplaces and children are in a hurry to reach their schools, so the roads are busy with people and vehicles.
  • Q: How do you travel to school?
    Ans: Sample answer: I travel to school in a school van. I make a queue to get on the van, sit on an empty seat, and keep sitting till the van stops.

While-reading

  • Q: Why are the black and white lines for crossing the road called zebra crossing?
    Ans: They are called a zebra crossing because the black and white lines painted on the road look like the black and white stripes of a zebra.
  • Q: Who runs carelessly on roads after school?
    Ans: After school, children run carelessly to cross the roads. This may cause accidents, so children should cross the road carefully.

Post Reading

  • Q: What are your duties on the road while travelling to school?
    Ans: My duties are to walk on the footpath, stop, look and cross the road from the zebra crossing, follow the traffic signal, make a queue to get on the van or bus, and obey the traffic rules and the traffic police.
  • Q: How will you cross the road if there are no traffic signals?
    Ans: I will follow the three steps: Step 1 — stand on the side of the road and look to my right. Step 2 — look to my left. Step 3 — look to my right again, and when the road is clear, cross the road from the zebra crossing.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking: Reading Comprehension

  • Q: What are the rules to cross a road?
    Ans: Stand on the side of the road and look to your right, then look to your left, then look to your right again and cross the road from the zebra crossing. Follow the traffic signal: cross the road when the light turns green and stop when it is red. Do not rush or run on the road and do not cross the road at turnings or bends.
  • Q: What will happen if we jump from a moving bus or a van?
    Ans: We can fall and get badly hurt in an accident. The book says we should never get down from a moving bus or van; we should keep sitting till the bus or van stops.
  • Q: How can we guide people to stop at the red light?
    Ans: We can tell them that the traffic signal must be followed: when the light is red we must stop, and we should cross or move only when the light turns green. We can also remind them that the traffic police control the vehicles on the roads and it is our duty to obey the traffic rules.
  • Q: What should we do when the yellow light is on?
    Ans: We should wait and get ready. In the poem 'Traffic Lights' in this unit, the yellow light says, 'start, start, right away', which means be ready — but we should actually go only when the light turns green.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the title of the story and the pictures next to it. What do you think the story is about?
    Ans: Sample answer: I think the story is about a boy who could not hear, and about a special day when everyone else also could not hear anything. The story tells us that such children should be treated just like any other children.

While-reading

  • Q: What did the people do on The Day of Silence?
    Ans: On The Day of Silence everyone put plugs in their ears, so they could not hear anything. The day was filled with fun, games and laughter, and people became aware of how different life was when they could not hear anything.

Post-reading

  • Q: Can you think of a different ending of this story?
    Ans: Sample answer: In a different ending, the villagers could learn some sign language after The Day of Silence, so that they could talk with Rizwan every day and he would never feel alone or different again.
  • Q: How should we treat the differently abled children at school/home?
    Ans: We should treat them just like any other children. We should help them, give them an equal chance, and not treat them as 'special' all the time, because everyone has some special talent. The story shows that Rizwan could do everything that the other little boys did.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking: Reading Comprehension

  • Q: Why was Rizwan liked by the villagers?
    Ans: Everyone in the village liked Rizwan for his good manners. He also actively took part in sports.
  • Q: What was the reason of Rizwan's unhappiness?
    Ans: His parents took extra care of him and accompanied him wherever they went out, and the other villagers also treated him as a special child. This made Rizwan feel unhappy, because he wanted to be treated like other boys.
  • Q: Who arranged the festival?
    Ans: Rizwan's close friend Mumtaz requested his father to arrange the festival, so Mumtaz's father arranged the festival in honour of the people who could not hear.
  • Q: Was The Day of Silence a special day for everyone?
    Ans: Yes, it was a special day for everyone. Everyone wore earplugs and could not hear anything, so people realized how different life is for a person who cannot hear. Rizwan won many games that day, and people realized that he should be treated just like any other little boy.

Sports and Games — Pre-reading

  • Q: What do you like to play with your friends?
    Ans: Sample answer: I like to play football and cricket with my friends in the playground. We also play local games like Pitthu Garam and Gulli Danda.
  • Q: Why are games important for everyone?
    Ans: Games are important because they develop good health and a sense of sharing. Children learn to participate and work in groups, they learn to accept victory and defeat, and sports help them to become leaders and teach them the value of time.

Sports and Games — While-reading

  • Q: Which game do you like to play with your mother / father?
    Ans: Sample answer: I like to play ludo with my mother and father. Ludo is an indoor game, and the text says we can play indoor games like ludo and carom with our parents and siblings.

Sports and Games — Post-reading

  • Q: How do you celebrate when you win a game or a competition?
    Ans: Sample answer: When our team wins a game, we cheer and clap together and say, 'Wonderful! Our team has won.' We feel happy and we thank all the team members.
  • Q: As a captain of a team, how do you motivate your team members when you lose a match?
    Ans: Sample answer: As a captain, I tell my team members not to lose heart. Games teach us to accept victory and defeat. I ask them to keep trying, to work together as a group and to play better in the next match.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — Reading Comprehension

  • Q: What is the passage type: a poem, a drama, a story, piece of information?
    Ans: The passage 'Sports and Games' is a piece of information. It gives us information about outdoor games, indoor games and the importance of playing games.
  • Q: There are four paragraphs in the text. Give a title to each one.
    Ans: Paragraph 1: 'Importance of Sports and Games'. Paragraph 2: 'Outdoor, Indoor and Family Games'. Paragraph 3: 'Playing in the Playground'. Paragraph 4: 'Learning to Interact and Lead'.
  • Q: What is the team celebrating at the end?
    Ans: At the end the team is celebrating its victory. The picture caption says, 'Wonderful! Our team has won.'
  • Q: Should we play games with the family members? Agree/disagree.
    Ans: Agree. We should play games with our family members. Indoor games like ludo and carom can be played with parents and siblings, a home becomes more cheerful through family games, and children learn a lot when they play with their elders.

Analytical Reading

  • Q: While playing cricket in the street, you hit the ball for a six. It smashes glass of a window. What will you do? i) run away and hide? ii) go to that house to say "sorry"? iii) make a new rule for playing in the street?
    Ans: I will choose option ii) — go to that house to say "sorry". Running away and hiding is dishonest. Saying sorry shows that I accept my mistake, and then I can also be careful while playing in the street in future.

Saving Resources — Pre-reading

  • Q: Why is it necessary to save natural resources?
    Ans: It is necessary to save natural resources because life would not have been possible without them. Many resources are being used more than the quantity of production, and the need for them has increased because of over population, so we need to conserve them.
  • Q: Do you know drinking clean water is necessary for health?
    Ans: Yes, drinking clean water is necessary for health. All need water to survive — humans, animals and plants — and water is essential for our life.

Saving Resources — While-reading

  • Q: How do you save water and electricity at school and home?
    Ans: Sample answer: I save water by turning off the tap while brushing my teeth and washing my hands, and I do not waste water while drinking from the cooler at school. I save electricity by turning off unnecessary lights and fans and by using natural light.

Saving Resources — Post-reading

  • Q: What will happen if we continue to waste water?
    Ans: If we continue wasting water, there will be acute shortage of it in the near future.
  • Q: Name the gifts of nature.
    Ans: The gifts of nature are air, water, land, sunlight, minerals, plants and animals.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — Reading Comprehension

  • Q: How can we avoid wasting water?
    Ans: We can avoid wasting water by checking water leakages in the house and school, by not taking a long shower, by turning off the tap while brushing teeth and washing hands, by not wasting water while drinking from the cooler at school, by watering the lawn and plants only when needed, and by washing cars with a bucket of water.
  • Q: Write two points to save electricity.
    Ans: Two points to save electricity are: 1) Turn off unnecessary lights. 2) Use natural light. (The text also says: unplug unused electronics, and switch off air conditioners when not at home.)
  • Q: What is paper made of?
    Ans: Paper is made of trees.
  • Q: How is environmental pollution caused?
    Ans: Environmental pollution is caused when trees are cut down, because cutting down trees pollutes the environment. We should make every effort not to pollute air, and we should plant more trees.

lessons.title: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Pre-reading

  • Q: Why do you think it is important to go out for a picnic with the family?
    Ans: Sample answer: It is important to go out for a picnic with the family because the family spends happy time together. In the dialogue in this unit, Majid went to a picnic with his family at Rawal Lake, Islamabad, and they enjoyed a lot.
  • Q: Will it be more fun if we go for picnic in spring?
    Ans: Sample answer: Yes, it will be more fun if we go for a picnic in spring, because the weather is pleasant in spring. Majid says in this unit that the weather was pleasant at Rawal Lake and they enjoyed a lot.

While-reading

  • Q: Did you ever have the same experience? (The family in the poem had its picnic ruined by rain, mosquitoes and bees.)
    Ans: Sample answer: No, I have never had the same experience. Whenever my family went out on a picnic, the weather was pleasant and we enjoyed a lot, like Majid's family at Rawal Lake.

Post-reading

  • Q: Do you think they could have checked the weather forecast?
    Ans: Yes, they could have checked the weather forecast. If they had checked it, they would have known that it was going to rain, and their picnic would not have been ruined.
  • Q: Why did they decide to go somewhere else next time?
    Ans: They decided to go somewhere else next time because their picnic was ruined by rain, mosquitoes and bees. The poem says: “So next time we'll go to the Café, or maybe just go to the mall.”

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension i. Read the text again in the beginning of the unit and answer the following questions

  • Q: Where did the family go on a picnic?
    Ans: The family went to the park on a picnic. The poem says: “My family went out on a picnic. We lugged all our stuff to the park.”
  • Q: What happened when they spread out the blanket?
    Ans: As soon as they'd spread out their blanket, it promptly got rainy and dark.
  • Q: Where did they decide to go for their entertainment in future?
    Ans: They decided to go to the Café, or maybe just to go to the mall, for their entertainment in future.
  • Q: How was their picnic ruined?
    Ans: Their picnic was ruined by the rain and the insects. It got rainy and dark, their napkins and plates blew away in the breeze, they were bit by mosquitoes and attacked by bees, and they ran screaming madly away and left all their stuff to the insects and rain that had ruined their day.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 2. Analytical Reading i. Read the questions and select one option out of three

  • Q: What is the author's purpose in writing this poem?
    Options: to amuse / to inform / to complain
    Ans: to amuse
  • Q: Do you think the author is:
    Options: pleased / sad / funny
    Ans: funny

Getting Started

  • Q: What do the pictures have in common?
    Ans: All the pictures show healthy habits of keeping ourselves clean. A boy is washing his hands, a boy is cutting his nails, a boy is brushing his teeth and a girl is combing her hair.

Pre-reading

  • Q: Look at the title of the lesson and guess what the text is about?
    Ans: The title is 'Toothy Toad'. The text is about a toad and his teeth, and about why we must look after our teeth.
  • Q: Why is it important to brush our teeth daily?
    Ans: It is important to brush our teeth daily to keep them clean and strong. Brushing removes dirt and germs from the teeth, so they do not decay and we do not get a toothache.

While-reading

  • Q: How many sweets do you eat in a day?
    Ans: Sample answer: I eat only one or two sweets in a day. I try to eat less, because eating too many sweets can decay my teeth.

Post-reading

  • Q: Why should we eat less candies?
    Ans: We should eat less candies because too many sweets decay our teeth. The decay spreads, holes are made in the teeth, the teeth start to fall out and we get a toothache, as happened with the toad in the story.
  • Q: Will we be healthy by taking care of our teeth?
    Ans: Yes, we will be healthy by taking care of our teeth. Clean and strong teeth help us to eat all sorts of foods well, to speak clearly and to smile happily.

B) Reading and Critical Thinking — 1. Reading Comprehension: i. Read the text again and answer the following questions

  • Q: Who would get perfect teeth?
    Ans: Whoever used the wizard's new spell would get perfect teeth.

  • Q: Why didn't the toad eat less sweets?
    Ans: The toad liked and enjoyed sweets so much that he didn't even try to eat less. He thought his teeth were too strong and he did not pay attention to the wizard's advice.
  • Q: How do you think the toad's teeth fell?
    Ans: One day a tooth started decaying and slowly the decay spread throughout his mouth. Soon there were holes in all his teeth and they started to fall out, because he ate too many sweets and did not brush his teeth.

lessons.title: Language Focus
lessons.notes_html:
C) Language Focus — 1. Vocabulary Building: I. Write the meanings of the given words and number of syllables in their respective columns

  • Q: Write the number of syllables and the meaning of 'event'.
    Ans: Number of syllables: 2 (e-vent). Meaning: something that happens, an important happening.
  • Q: Write the number of syllables and the meaning of 'please'.
    Ans: Number of syllables: 1 (please). Meaning: the polite word we use when we ask for something.
  • Q: Write the number of syllables and the meaning of 'picnic'.
    Ans: Number of syllables: 2 (pic-nic). Meaning: a trip on which food is taken and eaten outdoors.
  • Q: Write the number of syllables and the meaning of 'wizard'.
    Ans: Number of syllables: 2 (wiz-ard). Meaning: a man who does magic, as in the story 'Toothy Toad'.
  • Q: Write the number of syllables and the meaning of 'effort'.
    Ans: Number of syllables: 2 (ef-fort). Meaning: hard work done to do or get something.

1. Vocabulary Building: ii. Put the vocabulary words given above in alphabetical order

  • Q: Put the vocabulary words given above (event, please, picnic, wizard, effort) in alphabetical order.
    Ans: effort, event, picnic, please, wizard.

2. Learning to Spell: i. Fill in the blanks

  • Q: Fill in the blank: swe__t
    Ans: sweet — the missing letter is 'e'.
  • Q: Fill in the blank: catc__
    Ans: catch — the missing letter is 'h'.
  • Q: Fill in the blank: com__ands
    Ans: commands — the missing letter is 'm'.
  • Q: Fill in the blank: fr__end
    Ans: friend — the missing letter is 'i'.

3. Grammar: i. Fill in the blanks with 'wh' words

  • Q: ____ are you going?
    Ans: Where
  • Q: ____ is she playing now?
    Ans: What
  • Q: ____ will the school open?
    Ans: When

3. Grammar: ii. Write three countable nouns and three uncountable nouns from immediate surroundings in your notebook

  • Q: Write three countable nouns from your immediate surroundings.
    Ans: Sample answer: book, chair and pencil. These can be counted, so they are countable nouns.
  • Q: Write three uncountable nouns from your immediate surroundings.
    Ans: Sample answer: water, air and sand. These cannot be counted in numbers, so they are uncountable nouns.

3. Grammar: iii. You are a trainer of a parrot. Write four commands that you would give it

  • Q: Write command 1 that you would give to a parrot as its trainer.
    Ans: Come here.
  • Q: Write command 2 that you would give to a parrot as its trainer.
    Ans: Say hello.
  • Q: Write command 3 that you would give to a parrot as its trainer.
    Ans: Sit on my hand.
  • Q: Write command 4 that you would give to a parrot as its trainer.
    Ans: Fly and come back.

3. Grammar: iv. You are an instructor. The children are walking home from school. What two instructions will you give them so that they can reach home safely?

  • Q: Write instruction 1 for the children walking home from school, so that they can reach home safely.
    Ans: Walk on the side of the road and look at both sides carefully before crossing the road.
  • Q: Write instruction 2 for the children walking home from school, so that they can reach home safely.
    Ans: Go straight home together and do not talk to strangers on the way.

2. Creative Writing — Sequence writing: i. Complete the story of the picture in five sentences using the given words

  • Q: Complete the story of the picture in five sentences using the given words (First, Next, Then, After that, Last).
    Ans: First, a butterfly lays small eggs on a leaf. Next, a caterpillar comes out of the eggs and eats the leaf. Then, the caterpillar hangs from a twig and makes a hard cover around itself. After that, the cover opens and a butterfly comes out. Last, the beautiful butterfly flies away.
